challenge: Stateless MCP tasks and native desktop, scheduled, and inbox agents could resume after disconnection, but NodeKit had no portable owner-scoped contract proving which native agent, workspace, host, credential, and session generation was authorized to continue.
observedFailure: A label or fresh process could be mistaken for the same agent across restarts or hosts, while a continuity record could accidentally be treated as graph, review, or verdict authority.
resolution: Added immutable native-agent identity snapshots, exact host and credential bindings, single-generation rotation, short-lived content-addressed continuation grants, atomic consumed-once token enforcement with bounded abortable execution, explicit degraded read-only behavior, public schemas/types, and scenario-based replay and sustained-lineage tests. Caseflow, the stage-local graph, reviewer separation, and NodeProof retain their existing authority.
knownLimitations: Embedding applications own durable storage, atomic token-consumption transactions, and bounded retention.
Host and credential references require consumer-side issuer or attestation verification.
A provider outage permits only read-only display of a previously verified snapshot.
Consumer integration and production proofs remain separate from this portable package proof.
Canonical promotion requires a separately verified named-human approval.
